title: 2-SAT through implications and reachability
summary: Decide whether clauses with at most two literals have a model by comparing paths between opposite literals, then construct a model from an order of the components.
abstract: A clause with two literals can be read as two implications: when one literal is false, the other must be true. Following these implications turns satisfiability into a question about finite paths. Opposite literals cannot reach each other in both directions in any model. For clauses with at most two literals, this is also the only obstruction once empty clauses are excluded. The proof groups mutually reachable literals, orders the resulting classes, and chooses one of each pair of opposite classes to be true. An explicit invariant shows that the assignment respects every implication and therefore every clause. Worked examples connect this construction with unit propagation and show why empty clauses and the direction of the class order matter.
